key_insight: A distributed QAOA + classical repair pipeline can scale quantum-assisted Minimum Birkhoff Decomposition to thousand-variable problems by partitioning the task into hardware-feasible subproblems.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route for applying near-term quantum processors to large constrained optimization workloads in power systems, scheduling, and energy trading.
method: Spectrally partition the matching graph into smaller quantum subproblems.
Run single-layer QAOA sampling on each partition and repair infeasible samples classically.
Combine samples with E-FCFW optimization and spatial circuit packing to improve efficiency.
evidence_signal: On the PEGASE-1354 benchmark, repaired QAOA samples outperformed simulated annealing and uniform random baselines, and spatial circuit packing cut hardware execution time by about 3×.
watch_item: Performance depends on partition size and correlation retention; overly small partitions and aggressive MPS truncation can weaken candidate quality and convergence.
paper_title: Scaling Quantum Optimization to the Thousand-Qubit Scale with Distributed Quantum Sampling
